terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here and print what busiest_hill sees as it goes.

tasks.title: The smallest log that goes wrong
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `busiest_hill.py`, write a function called `smallest_failing` that takes nothing and gives back a list of hills, a log, for which `busiest_hill` as it came with the file gives back the wrong hill: not the hill with the most callouts, or on a tie not the one that came first in the log. The log must have as few callouts as a log can have and still go wrong. Find it by cutting `month` down: take out one callout at a time, and keep each cut while the answer is still wrong.

Check calls `smallest_failing` and asks its own copy of `busiest_hill`, as it came with the file, and a mended copy about the log it gives back. The answers must differ, and no shorter log can make them differ.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on cutting the input down.
Give back a copy of month from smallest_failing for now. At the bottom of the file, below busiest_hill, print what busiest_hill gives back for smallest_failing().
Take out one callout, print again, and count by hand which hill is right. Keep the cut only while the answer is still wrong.
When every callout you could take out makes the answer right, give that list back from smallest_failing.
hints: A wrong answer is one that differs from what you count by hand. Count each hill's callouts in your list, and on a tie take the hill that comes first.
Try taking out callouts from the start, the middle and the end. The log goes wrong only while some hills keep a certain number of callouts each: notice which hills matter.
A log stays wrong with three different hills: one that comes first with one callout, then two others with more callouts than it. The shape is `return [...]` with five hills in it.

tasks.title: Mend busiest_hill
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, `busiest_hill` takes a list of hills, a log with at least one callout, and should give back the hill with the most callouts, and on a tie the one that came first in the log. It gives back the wrong hill for `month`, without an error. Find the mistake and mend it. Print the names and values it works with as it goes, to see where they stop being right.

Check calls `busiest_hill` with logs of its own, ties among them, and looks at the hill it gives back.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on printing names and values.
Run busiest_hill on your smallest log from Task 1, not on the whole month.
In the second loop, print hill, counts[hill], most and best on each round.
Find the name that does not change when it should, and mend that line.
hints: The counting in the first loop is right: print `counts` after it to see. The mistake is in how the best hill is chosen.
`most` is meant to be the number of callouts of the best hill so far. Print it on each round of the second loop: does it change when `best` does?
When a hill becomes the new `best`, `most` has to become its count too: add `most = counts[hill]` under `best = hill`.

tasks.title: Say what must be true
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, the comment asks for one line in `busiest_hill`, above it under `# Task 2`. `busiest_hill` is never meant to be asked about a log with no callouts. Add an `assert` as its first line, stating that the list it is given is not empty, so that an empty list stops it right there with `AssertionError`. A log with callouts still works as before.

Check calls `busiest_hill` with an empty list, where `AssertionError` must reach Check, and with logs that have callouts.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on assert.
Call busiest_hill([]) as it is, and read the error it stops with today, and where.
Write an assert as the first line of busiest_hill, with something after it that is False for an empty list.
Call busiest_hill([]) again and read the new error.
hints: Today an empty list stops with an `IndexError` on the line that reads `hills[0]`, which says nothing about why.
`assert` followed by a condition stops with `AssertionError` when the condition is False. Leave out round brackets around the condition and its message: they make a tuple, which is always true.
The shape is `assert len(hills) > 0, "busiest_hill was given an empty log"` as the first line inside `busiest_hill`.
